title: BEAUT uncovers new gut-microbial bile-acid enzymes and the novel bile acid 3-acetoDCA
summary: The BEAUT workflow combines ESM-2 protein-language-model embeddings with a neural classifier and active-site-pocket-similarity data augmentation to search gut microbial proteins for bile-acid enzymes. The authors predicted over 600,000 candidate enzymes and experimentally tested selected predictions; assays identified new bile-acid activities including MABH and ADS. ADS produces 3-acetoDCA, a previously undescribed bile-acid carbon skeleton, reported in human feces and shown to alter microbial composition and promote Lactobacillus-associated effects in experimental studies.
ai_technology: BEAUT, ESM-2 protein-language-model embeddings plus dense neural-network classifier, augmented using active-site-pocket similarity
organization: Peking University; Peking University Third Hospital; Tsinghua–Peking University Joint Center for Life Sciences; Nanchang University

evidence.tested: The authors predicted over 600,000 candidate enzymes and experimentally tested selected predictions; assays identified new bile-acid activities including MABH and ADS.
evidence.unknown: The 600,000 figure is a prediction set, not experimentally characterized enzymes; authors tested selected subsets. Physiological claims are based on study assays and animal/microbial experiments, not demonstrated human clinical effects. The journal full text was inaccessible in this reader; the Peking University research team's detailed release summarizes its Cell paper, methods and experiments.
evidence.ai_role: Screened microbial protein sequences for likely bile-acid-metabolizing function and prioritized candidate enzymes; experimental characterization of selected AI predictions identified enzyme activities and the ADS/3-acetoDCA pathway.
